entry.title: Weird JS
entry.summary:
null vs undefined in JavaScript
1. undefined: Variable declared but not assigned. 2. null: Variable intentionally set to no value.
let a; console.log(a); // undefined
let b = null; console.log(b); // null
Summary: undefined = automatic (I haven't given a value yet) null = intentional (I specifically have no value)

entry.summary: If you are building modern systems, you have probably heard this question: “How do access-first systems compare to FIDO2 Passkeys?” That question assumes they are solving the same problem. Passkeys improve authentication. Understanding the difference matters if you care about system boundaries, attack surface, and long-term maintainability — not just login UX. FIDO2 Passkeys were designed to eliminate passwords. They remove shared secrets, resist phishing attacks, and reduce credential reuse.
